title: When does the dew appear?
hook: An evening cools; the air keeps its water. When does the grass get wet?

knows: that dew forms on cool mornings
doesNotKnow: that relative humidity compares the water in the air with a maximum that depends on temperature
that cooling lowers that maximum until it meets the water already there (the dew point)

misconception: Relative humidity measures how much water is in the air, whatever the temperature, so cooling does not change it.
objective: The learner can explain that air at 30 °C and 50% relative humidity holds 2.12 kPa of water vapour, which is the full maximum at about 18 °C, so cooling it to about 18 °C brings it to 100% and dew forms.

claims.text: The most water vapour that can stay vapour rises steeply with temperature; at 30 °C it is about 4.24 kPa.
claims.source: Magnus formula es(T) = 0.61094 exp(17.625 T / (T + 243.04)) kPa (Alduchov & Eskridge 1996, J. Appl. Meteor. 35: 601-609); es(30) = 4.237 kPa (node). CRC Handbook 'Vapor pressure of water': 4.247 kPa at 30 °C.

claims.text: Relative humidity is the water vapour in the air as a share of the most that can stay vapour at that temperature.
claims.source: WMO Guide to Instruments and Methods of Observation (WMO-No. 8), relative humidity as ratio of vapour pressure to saturation vapour pressure.

claims.text: Air at 30 °C and 50% relative humidity holds about 2.12 kPa of water vapour, which is the full maximum at about 18 °C, so dew first forms at about 18 °C (the dew point).
Below the dew point the extra water condenses as dew, so the vapour that remains is the full maximum for that temperature.
claims.source: Definition of dew point (WMO-No. 8; American Meteorological Society Glossary, 'dew point'). The stage keeps the air's total water fixed and ignores pressure changes on cooling (small). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Matches the stage model (vapour = min(E, es(t)), excess shown as dew) and the AMS Glossary definition of dew point (saturation on cooling at constant pressure and water content). Assumes equilibrium (no supersaturation), as the stage does.

recall.question: A cold drink from the fridge gets wet on the outside on a humid day. Why?
options: air touching the glass cools below its dew point, so its water vapour condenses
the cold makes new water from the air's oxygen
recall.why: Cooling the air next to the glass lowers the most vapour it can keep; below the dew point the extra water condenses on the glass.
